spec: Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid representing the original rotated 180 degrees (equivalent to reversing the order of the rows and reversing each row). The grid may be any size, including a single row, a single column, or empty, in which case an empty grid is returned.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list containing the sum of each row, in order from the first row to the last. Rows may contain negative numbers or zeros, and if the grid has no rows return an empty list.

Given a 2D grid of integers with at least one row (all rows the same length), return a list containing the sum of each column, in order from the first column to the last. If the grid is empty or its rows are empty, return an empty list.

Given a 2D grid of integers, a row index r, a column index c, and a target value, count how many of the (up to four) orthogonal neighbours of cell (r, c) - above, below, left, and right - are within the bounds of the grid and equal to the target value. Cells on an edge or corner simply have fewer neighbours to check.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of the elements on its main diagonal, that is grid[0][0], grid[1][1], grid[2][2], and so on, stopping once either the rows or the columns run out. The grid need not be square. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of the elements on its anti-diagonal, running from the top-right corner to the bottom-left, that is grid[0][cols-1], grid[1][cols-2], and so on, stopping once either the rows or the columns run out. The grid need not be square. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of its elements visited in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner: across the top row, down the right column, back across the bottom row, up the left column, and then spiraling inward, repeating until every cell has been visited exactly once. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.
Given a 2D grid whose cells are strings, and a target string value, count how many cells in the entire grid are equal to that value. If the grid is empty, or the value never appears, return 0.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a list of the values of all the cells that lie on the border of the grid (the first row, the last row, the first column, or the last column), listed in row-major order (row by row, left to right within each row). If the grid has only one row or one column, every cell is a border cell. Return an empty list if the grid is empty or has no columns.

Given two 2D grids of integers, determine whether the second grid can be obtained from the first by rotating it by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees. Return True if any of those four rotations of the first grid equals the second grid exactly (same dimensions and same values in the same positions), and False otherwise. Two empty grids are considered equal.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a single flat list containing all of its elements in row-major order (the first row's elements in order, then the second row's, and so on). If the grid has no rows, or all rows are empty, return an empty list.
Given a 2D grid of integers, possibly containing negative numbers, return the sum of every element in the grid. If the grid has no rows, or all rows are empty, return 0.

Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers with at least one cell, return a tuple (row, col) giving the position of the maximum value in the grid. If the maximum value occurs more than once, return the position of its first occurrence when scanning row by row, left to right.

Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers where every row has at least one element, return the index of the row whose elements sum to the largest total. If more than one row ties for the largest sum, return the smallest such index.

Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers with at least one column, return the index of the column whose elements sum to the largest total. If more than one column ties for the largest sum, return the smallest such index.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid in which the order of the elements within each row is reversed, but the order of the rows themselves is unchanged. Rows may have different lengths, and an empty grid should produce an empty grid.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return a new grid in which the order of the rows is reversed (the first row becomes the last and vice versa), while the elements within each row stay in their original order. An empty grid should produce an empty grid.

Given a 2D grid of integers and a threshold value, count how many cells in the grid contain a value strictly greater than the threshold. Negative thresholds and negative grid values are both allowed, and an empty grid should give a count of 0.

Given a square 2D grid of integers, return the sum of all elements on its main diagonal plus all elements on its anti-diagonal. If the grid has an odd size, the single center cell (which lies on both diagonals) must be counted only once, not twice.

Given a 2D grid of 0s and 1s, where 0 marks an open cell and 1 marks a blocked obstacle, count the number of distinct paths from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell that move only right or down at each step, without ever entering a blocked cell. If the starting cell or the destination cell is itself blocked, return 0.

Given a 2D grid containing only the integers 0 and 1, count the number of separate islands, where an island is a group of 1-cells connected to each other horizontally or vertically (not diagonally). If the grid contains no 1-cells, or the grid is empty, return 0.

Given a 2D grid of integers, a starting row sr, a starting column sc, and a new value, perform a flood fill: replace the value at (sr, sc) and every cell reachable from it through horizontally or vertically adjacent cells of the same original value with the new value, and return the resulting grid as a new grid (the input grid must not be modified). If the new value is the same as the value already at (sr, sc), return a copy of the grid unchanged.
Given a 2D grid of integers, return the number of distinct values that appear anywhere in the grid. An empty grid, or a grid whose rows are all empty, has 0 distinct values.

Given a square 2D grid of integers, return the trace of the matrix, defined as the sum of the elements on its main diagonal (grid[0][0] + grid[1][1] + ... ). An empty grid (zero rows) has a trace of 0.

Given a 2D grid of integers, determine whether it looks identical after being rotated 180 degrees, meaning grid[i][j] equals grid[rows-1-i][cols-1-j] for every cell. Return True if this holds for every cell (including for an empty grid), and False otherwise.

Given a 2D grid of integers, return the sum of the values of all cells that lie on the border of the grid (the first row, the last row, the first column, or the last column). If the grid has only one row or one column, every cell counts as a border cell. Return 0 if the grid is empty or has no columns.

Given a 2D grid of integers and two values old and new, return a new grid (the input grid must not be modified) in which every cell equal to old has been replaced by new, and all other cells are unchanged. If old never appears in the grid, the returned grid must have the same values as the input.

Given a 2D grid of integers, count how many of its rows read the same forwards and backwards (are palindromes). A row with zero or one elements always counts as a palindrome. An empty grid has 0 palindromic rows.

Given a 2D grid of integers, count how many of its columns, read from top to bottom, read the same forwards and backwards (are palindromes). A column with zero or one elements always counts as a palindrome. Return 0 if the grid is empty or has no columns.

Given two 2D grids of integers a and b representing matrices, where a has dimensions m by n and b has dimensions n by p, return their matrix product as a new m by p grid, computed using standard matrix multiplication. Assume the number of columns of a always matches the number of rows of b.

Given a 2D grid of integers and a target value, return a tuple (row, col) giving the position of the first cell (scanning row by row, left to right) whose value equals the target. If the target value does not appear anywhere in the grid, return None.

Given a non-empty 2D grid of integers with at least one row and one column, return the sum of the values at its four corners: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. If the grid has only one row or one column, some corners coincide with each other, but each of the four corner positions must still be added, so a coinciding value is counted more than once.
